items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: Emerson I always thought was an excellent leader. He was a very dogmatic guy — a my way or the highway kind of guy — very much in control, which I think is good in a leader.

ctx.x: Tell me a little bit about playing with Emerson and what was he like back then?

Emerson I always thought was an excellent leader. He was a very dogmatic guy — a my way or the highway kind of guy — very much in control, which I think is good in a leader. Certainly as a young guy who’d never done this kind of stuff before it was very helpful to be told what to do and how to do it and all of that. Emerson was also very nice to me. He helped me with some of my studies and I always — when you’re sort of new and unknown and somebody helps you get over the rough spots you always remember those…

I thought he was a great leader and I think a lot of the success of the band was due to his musical leadership, to Donny’s wonderful ability to do all the behind the scenes stuff, and to these just killer drummers who just drove us at these tempos that would just knock your socks off. So I think those three things had a lot to do with it.
